solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fondle a thicker thong?

definitions.meaning: to fondle is to feel someone up, to paw or touch them clumsily
a G-string is a skimpy thong, so a thicker one, made of something heavier than string

explanation.surface: A bawdy question about underwear and wandering hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a joke: a thong is a G-string, and something thicker than string is rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Groping is fumbling or feeling over someone's body, a close synonym for handling them amorously.

clue.text: Diminutive fixer employing son in catering team?

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the team holds this letter

parts.note: grub is food, so a grub crew is jokily a catering team

explanation.surface: A small handyman hired with his son by a catering firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub screw is a small headless screw, a tiny fastener that fixes parts together.

clue.text: Odd bits lopped from bonsai pear tree

indicators.note: lopping the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones of these words

explanation.surface: Pruning a bonsai pear tree by snipping off bits.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a small willow grown for basketwork, so it is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Monstrosity setter picked out in speech

indicators.note: in speech tells us to go by how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: the setter is I, and picked out means saw

explanation.surface: A setter selected an ugly thing during a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a near match in a non-rhotic accent, where the final R is not voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, so a monstrosity of a building is one.

clue.text: Sentimental bit of guff inserted in curtailed codicil at son's homecoming

indicators.note: inserted in says one piece is put inside another
coming home is coming back, so the stretch of letters is read backwards
curtailed tells us to cut away the start of codicil and the end of son's, keeping only the letters in between
a bit of guff is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A sentimental scene: a will's codicil read out as a son returns home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' trims the phrase 'codicil at son's' to CILATSON; 'homecoming' turns it back to NOSTALIC, and the G from 'bit of guff' is 'inserted in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgic feelings are wistful, sentimental longings for the past, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Found on the stairs prying?

definitions.meaning: the rounded front edge of each step tread, overhanging the riser
poking about in other people's business

explanation.definitionFit: A nosing is the projecting edge of a stair tread, and nosing about is snooping or interfering.

clue.text: Problem with hair being entangled — see what tangle can do!

definitions.meaning: a frayed tip where a strand of hair has divided

definitions.text: being entangled — see what tangle can do!
definitions.meaning: in the word entangled, tangle sits between EN and D, so tangle can divide the word end

explanation.surface: Tangled hair causes damage, as anyone with knots knows.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is wordplay on the word itself: 'entangled' is 'end' parted to hold 'tangle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Split ends are frayed hair tips where the strand divides, a common hair-care complaint.

clue.text: 10 has a record-player: posh, new and about time

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, plays records
U means upper-class
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A joint has a turntable, plus something posh and new, and timing.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is JOINT in the sense of something attached or associated.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjunct is an attached or associated thing, and joint likewise describes things linked together.

clue.text: Sliding about so erratically, one's fallen

definitions.text: Sliding about so erratically, one's fallen

indicators.note: erratically means wildly, so these letters are jumbled
fallen means dropped, so one of the letters goes

parts.note: taken as written
one is I, the Roman numeral
A, taken as the short form of about, the rest of the word falling away
taken as written

explanation.surface: A skater slides wildly about and takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a musical slide; the blog takes 'about' as A, the rest of the word dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid glide up or down a scale, a musical sliding between notes.

clue.text: Unhappy with pins?

definitions.meaning: pins are legs, and up with pins suggests something cut is ready to be pinned up, as dressmakers do

explanation.definitionFit: To be cut up about something is British informal for being very distressed or upset.

clue.text: Journalist Vine's unsettled: 'I may move in several directions'

definitions.text: I may move in several directions

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of journalist and Vine, the possessive adding none

explanation.surface: A journalist called Vine is rattled and threatens to wander off in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Vine is a BBC journalist and presenter; the possessive 's adds no letter to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A universal joint is a coupling letting a shaft turn through any angle, so it can move in several directions.

clue.text: See 9
Knight's move for Latino failing at 10

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

indicators.note: to move the remaining letters is to rearrange them
failing means missing, so the word at drops out of Latino

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chess problem: a knight's move goes wrong for a Latino player.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is the cross-reference to JOINT, and a sirloin is a joint of beef; 'move' is not the chess sense but an instruction to rearrange LINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirloin is a prime cut of beef roasted whole, an example of a meat joint.

clue.text: Tweaks on the fiddle?

parts.note: suggests minor cheating or fraud, but describes a violinist adjusting the pegs to get the strings in pitch

explanation.surface: Small adjustments made while on the fiddle, as in a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' is British slang for cheating; here the fiddle is a violin being adjusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing an instrument to correct pitch is tuning it, and tweaking an engine is also tuning it.

clue.text: 10 to pass back and forth across Spain

indicators.note: across says one piece lies over the other, here wrapped around it
back and forth tells us the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: to refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Kicking a ball to and fro across Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is JOINT in its slang sense of a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is slang for a cannabis cigarette, which is also called a joint.

clue.text: Rigour from former thespian with name for resistance

indicators.note: with one thing for another tells us to swap letters

parts.note: an ex-actress is a former actress
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A retired actor changes her name for the sake of rigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With name for resistance' swaps N in for the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness is precision and strictness, which is what rigour in work means.

clue.text: See 19
10's unfortunate glitch in centre

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the centre

parts.note: the nub is the centre or core of something

indicators.note: unfortunate is a sign the letters have come out badly ordered

explanation.surface: An unlucky glitch at the heart of the operation.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is JOINT in its slang sense of a seedy venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint is slang for a bar or club, so a nightclub is one example of such a place.

clue.text: Unreliable lover (Paris) is escaping censure

indicators.note: unreliable means not to be trusted, so these letters are rearranged
escaping means getting out, so those letters leave the name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fickle lover in Paris avoids being blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is escaping' takes IS out of PARIS to leave PAR, which joins LOVER to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproval is a rebuke or scolding, the same thing as censure.

clue.text: Most theatrical time's wasted after opening in wretched shockers

indicators.note: after puts the trimmed word behind the first letter
the opening in a word is its first letter
wasted means lost, so that letter is removed

parts.note: hammiest means the most over-acted, like a ham actor
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A melodramatic actor's wasted time amid dreadful flops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time's wasted' drops T from HAMMIEST to leave HAMMIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Whammies are nasty blows or setbacks, informal synonyms for shockers.

clue.text: 10 is in Death In Venice and 10 (now showing)

indicators.note: in says this piece goes inside the next

parts.note: in Venice the Italian for death is morte
taken as written
taken as written
the second 10 is just the number ten
on means being shown, like a film

explanation.surface: Film listings: Death in Venice and Ten are now showing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second '10' is not the cross-reference but the number, and 'Death In Venice' tells you to translate into Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortise and tenon is a classic woodworking connection, one peg fitted into a slot.

clue.text: Skirt with shirt for advanced rank

indicators.note: with one thing for another tells us to swap letters

parts.note: a sarong is a wrapped skirt from South-East Asia
T for a T-shirt

explanation.surface: Swapping a skirt for a shirt lands someone a higher rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With shirt for advanced' swaps T in for the A of SARONG; 'rank' is the adjective, as in a rank smell, not a military grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank smell is a strong one: both mean powerful and offensive in odour or taste.

clue.text: Story recounted to completion in Charlie's place?

indicators.note: recounted means told, so it is the spoken sound that matters

parts.note: a tale is a story
the end is completion

explanation.surface: A story told right to its finish in Charlie's home.
explanation.walkthrough: A tail-end Charlie is the rear gunner of a bomber, or the last in a line, so Charlie's place is at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase tail-end Charlie names whoever comes last, so the rear is that person's position.

clue.text: 10's article appearing in 8

indicators.note: appearing in says this piece sits inside the other

parts.note: 8 down means cut up, as is to shred
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article from a joint appears in a cut-up form.
explanation.walkthrough: '10's' reads as 'joint is', with joint the adjective: common to more than one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held jointly is held in common, divided between people.

clue.text: Decapitated sewer rat decomposing in vessel

indicators.note: decomposing means breaking down, so the letters are rearranged
with its head cut off, the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A grisly find: a headless rat rotting in a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterer is a container used for supplying water to animals or plants, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: 10 having periodic worries on Tuesday first thing

indicators.note: on puts one piece next to the other
periodic means at regular intervals, picking the alternating letters
first thing is the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone smokes a joint to calm regular worries first thing on Tuesday.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint between hand and forearm is the carpal one at the base of the hand.

clue.text: Shed medium bit of 'corporation' getting in trim

indicators.note: getting in says these letters go inside the shed

parts.note: a hut is a small shed
air is the medium through which sound travels

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A company shed some staff in a cost-cutting trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a verb but is the noun HUT; 'corporation' also hints at a paunch, misdirecting toward weight loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A trim at the barber's is a light haircut, so the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Be wary about perhaps reading what one does to 10

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, a schoolboy warning
reading is one of the three Rs, so R

explanation.surface: Beware: reading may be what you do to a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; 'perhaps' flags R as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: At a Sunday roast one slices meat from a joint, which is the verb for cutting it up.

clue.text: Celts are among prehistoric enigmas

indicators.note: among says the letters sit amid the following words

explanation.surface: Celtic peoples are among the riddles of prehistory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe in East Anglia, led by Boudica in revolt against Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a Celtic tribe of ancient Britain, so they are an example of Celts.

clue.text: Revelations held back by Albert when editing this column

indicators.note: by puts one piece next to the other
held back tells us the word is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is the abbreviation for the Book of Revelation

indicators.note: editing reworks the name's letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Albert edits a newspaper column but holds back some revelations.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the adjective: the spine is the vertebral column, so 'this column' points at the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The backbone is called the vertebral column, so the adjective names that particular spinal column.

clue.text: Thanks to second push, Edward's decorated

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
to push a product is to sell it hard
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward gets a decoration thanks to one more push.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasselled means trimmed with tassels, a kind of ornamented or adorned finish.

clue.text: Wally and his cap found in river by bishop

indicators.note: found in says this letter lies inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: his cap is the top, the capital letter of the word Wally

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A fool's hat is fished from the river by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wally' is British slang for a fool; it does double duty, giving its capital W too.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a boring, socially inept person, a near synonym of the slang word for a silly fool.
